messages:
alex.h: Heads up — found a plaintext AWS access key in external-ingest webhook logs from partner X. Key id ends with: 9K7X. Looks like an old long-lived svcacc key. Posting minimal context here, will DM full log to @sarah.

security-bot: Alert SEC-2026-042 created, evidence saved to secure incident folder (s3://redwood-secure/incidents/SEC-2026-042).

sarah: Thanks. Can you paste the redacted log line (masking the secret) and the S3 object path? We need to scope blast radius.

alex.h: ``
2026-03-23T15:07:12Z INFO webhook.ingest partner=partner-x file=s3://partner-uploads/2026/03/23/abc.log key_id=AKIA************9K7X status=OK
``
Object: s3://partner-uploads/2026/03/23/abc.log (we pulled a small sample).

jordan: I'm taking ownership of immediate containment. Plan: 1) revoke the exposed key in AWS, 2) pause partner ingestion jobs, 3) rotate any KMS wrapping keys if they cover this object, 4) reissue short-lived creds. @ops-oncall can you pause ingestion now?

ops-oncall: Pausing — scaling deployment ingress-consumer-partner-x -> 0 now. Command: `kubectl -n ingest scale deploy/ingress-consumer-partner-x --replicas=0` ; confirmed pause at 15:12 UTC.

sarah: Good. Jordan, revoke command for AWS (if it's an IAM user key): `aws iam update-access-key --user-name ingest-partner-x --access-key-id AKIA...9K7X --status Inactive` then `aws iam delete-access-key ...` after verification. Also run `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=AccessKeyId,AttributeValue=AKIA...9K7X` to capture usage timestamps. Save output to evidence bucket.

emily: I'll check Vault and KMS mappings. Possible exposures: 1) transit-wrapping key for partner backups, 2) any vault kv mounts where that key was stored. Running: `vault list secret/partners/partner-x` and `gcloud kms keys list --location=global --keyring=partner-x` (if GCP KMS used). Will post findings.

jordan: If re-wrap needed: we should create a new wrapping key and re-encrypt stored ciphertexts in a rolling manner. Minimal impact window approach: rewrap on read + background job to rewrap stored blobs. Owner: emily.

sarah: Also enable high-retention audit logs: enable object-level auditing for the S3 bucket and increase Vault audit log retention for 30d for this incident. Preserve logs before deleting anything.

emily: Found a transit key grant that includes a role used by partner-x. Marking it for rekey. I will: 1) create new transit key `partner-x-transit-v2`, 2) add binding for our internal rewrap-runner, 3) schedule rewrap job. ETA for key creation + test rewrap: 2 hours.

jordan: Owner assignments: jordan -> revoke AWS key + cloudtrail evidence; emily -> transit key rekey + rewrap; sarah -> RBAC audit and retention policy adjust; alex.h -> provide full log export and sample. Timeline: immediate actions done in 0-30m, rewrap & rotation 1-4h, full audit & closure within 24h.

ops-oncall: Note: paused ingestion. Will stand by to unpause once new creds are live.

alex.h: Uploaded redacted full log and sample to secure incident folder and DM'd @sarah the raw snippet.

sarah: Thanks — once rewrap job starts, mark the incident channel and we’ll run a regression test on ingestion in staging then do a canary in prod.

emily: Starting key creation now. Will post `request_id` and test vector.

jordan: After revoke, run RBAC search: `gcloud projects get-iam-policy redwood-prod --flatten="bindings[]" --filter="bindings.members:serviceAccount:ingest-partner-x@"` to find incidental bindings.

sarah: Also check for any Terraform state or CI artifacts that may have the key: `git grep --break --heading -n "AKIA"` in repos flagged for partner integrations. If found, rotate those too.

jordan: All right, moving to action. Keep updates here. :thumbsup:

security-bot: Incident status updated -> containment in progress. Evidence frozen and snapshot created.
